title: Charm Quark — Identity and Quantum Numbers
description: The Charm quark carries: electric charge +2/3 e, spin 1/2, generation 2, and one of three color charges (red, green, blue). Its mass is ~1.28 GeV/c^2. Quark masses are scheme-dependent (quoted in the MS-bar scheme); the charge and quantum numbers are exact.
how_it_works: Quantum numbers are the quark's identity card: charge, spin, color, flavor, generation. Every hadron's charge and mass trace back to these numbers.

title: Charm Quark — Hadrons Formed
description: Quarks never appear alone; the Charm quark appears bound in: J/psi (c anti-c), D+ (c anti-d), D0 (c anti-u), Lambda_c+ (udc).
how_it_works: Hadron composition is deterministic: sum the quark charges for the hadron's charge, sum constituent masses for a mass estimate (binding energy excluded). The demo verifies this.
key_points: Hadrons: J/psi (c anti-c), D+ (c anti-d), D0 (c anti-u), Lambda_c+ (udc)

title: Charm Quark — Interactions and Decays
description: Weak decays to strange/down quarks (c -> s + W+); J/psi (c anti-c) was the discovery channel; D mesons (c + light quark) show CP violation studies.
how_it_works: Three forces act on quarks: the strong force binds them (gluons), the weak force changes their flavor, electromagnetism acts on their charge. Flavor change is the only way a quark becomes another quark.

title: Charm Quark — Confinement and Color
description: No free quark has ever been seen: the strong force grows with distance, so quarks are permanently confined in color-neutral hadrons (baryons: three colors; mesons: color-anticolor). Pull hard enough and the energy creates new quarks instead of freeing one.
how_it_works: Confinement is why the demo composes hadrons rather than isolating quarks — the hadron is the observable unit.
key_points: Energy creates pairs, never free quarks

title: Charm Quark — Mass Scale
description: The Charm quark's mass (~1.28 GeV/c^2) sets its role: light quarks (u, d, s) build everyday matter; heavy quarks (c, b, t) are collider physics. The top quark's ~172.7 GeV mass — heavier than a tungsten atom — makes it the only 'natural' quark mass, with a Higgs coupling near 1.
how_it_works: Masses are compared in MeV/c^2; the six flavors span five orders of magnitude — the flavor puzzle the Standard Model does not explain.
key_points: Mass origin: the Higgs mechanism (unexplained pattern)
